column1: # TITLE: Identification of differentially expressed genes using microarray analysis and COL6A1 induction of bone metastasis in non-small cell lung cancer
# SUMMARY: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a major cause of cancer-associated mortality worldwide
column2: and bone metastasis is the most prevalent event observed in patients with advanced NSCLC. However
column3: the pathogenesis of bone metastases has not been fully elucidated. In the present study
column4: differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified by gene expression microarray analysis of NSCLC tissue samples with or without bone metastases. Subsequently
column5: collagen family collagen 6A1 (COL6A1) was chosen as the target gene through Ingenuity Pathway Analysis and reverse transcription-quantitative (RT-q)PCR validation of the top eight DEGs. COL6A1 was overexpressed or knocked down
column6: and the proliferation and invasion of NSCLC cells was assessed using Cell Counting Kit-8
column7: colony formation and Transwell invasion assays. Additionally
column8: the osteogenic capacity of HOB and hES-MP 002.5 cells was assessed using RT-qPCR
column10: Alizarin Red staining and alkaline phosphatase staining. A total of 364 DEGs were identified in NSCLC tissues with bone metastases compared with NSCLC tissues without bone metastases
column11: including 140 upregulated genes and 224 downregulated genes. Gene Ontology analysis indicated that the upregulated and downregulated genes were primarily enriched in ‘cellular process’
column12: ‘metabolic process’ and ‘biological regulation’. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes pathway enrichment analysis revealed that the upregulated genes were primarily enriched in ‘cysteine and methionine metabolism’
column14: while the downregulated genes were primarily enriched in ‘transcriptional mis-regulation in cancer’
column15: ‘ribosome’ and ‘mitophagy in animals’. COL6A1 was highly expressed in NSCLC tissue samples with bone metastases. Functionally
column16: COL6A1 overexpression induced the proliferation and invasion of HARA cells
column17: and knockdown prevented the proliferation and invasion of HARA-B4 cells. Finally
column18: it was demonstrated that HOB and hES-MP 002.5 cells exhibited osteogenic capacity
column19: and overexpression of COL6A1 in HARA cells increased adhesion of these cells to the osteoblasts
column20: whereas knockdown of COL6A1 in HARA-B4 cells reduced their adhesive ability. In conclusion
column21: COL6A1 may serve as a potential diagnostic marker and therapeutic target for bone metastasis in NSCLC.
